paper.title_en: Field of duality: a dual-quaternion framework for wave dynamics in Bose-Einstein condensates and analogue Hawking radiation
paper.abstract_en: We present the Field of Duality ($\mathrm {F.D.}$) as a phenomenological dual-quaternion framework for coupled wave systems with an intrinsic length scale. Starting from a compact algebraic constraint on a dual-quaternion field, we derive coupled scalar-vector wave equations with two free parameters: a coupling constant $\gamma $ (where Hermiticity of the wave operator requires $\alpha =\beta \equiv \gamma $) and a duality length L. The dispersion relation is analytically identical to the Bogoliubov spectrum of weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) under the unique identification $\gamma =1/2$ and $L=\xi $ (the healing length). This equivalence is exact at the level of analytic expressions and extends to all orders in the momentum expansion. The non-trivial result is that such an equivalence exists: within the model class defined by Axiom-1-Axiom-5-in particular the restriction to second-order spatial derivatives (Axiom-3)-the dual-quaternion algebraic structure (via Proposition 1 ) forces the dispersion to the functional form $\omega ^2 = c^2k^2(1+\gamma L^2k^2)$, with no $k^6$ or higher-order terms-exactly the Bogoliubov functional form-making the parameter matching not merely possible but structurally inevitable within the axiom class. Extending this framework to sonic horizons, we obtain thermal corrections to analogue Hawking radiation with coefficients $(\gamma _0,\gamma _1)=(0.0074\pm 0.0004,-0.0011\pm 0.0002)$, predicting characteristic $\eta ^2$ scaling. This differs from the $\eta ^3$ scaling of conventional asymmetric Bogoliubov-de Gennes treatments, reflecting the symmetric coupling enforced by the $\mathrm {F.D.}$ algebraic structure. The associated deviations from the Planck spectrum are of order 0.2-$1.2\%$ for realistic $^{87}$ Rb parameters. Experimental measurement of the scaling exponent would test whether the $\mathrm {F.D.}$ symmetry is physically realized at sonic horizons. The framework demonstrates that dual quaternions provide a minimal algebraic structure capable of encoding coupled wave dynamics with intrinsic scales. This phenomenological approach complements microscopic derivations by providing an algebraic route to coupled wave equations with intrinsic length scales, suggesting new avenues for geometric approaches to continuum physics.
